name: Saddle shoes

lead: Saddle shoes are low-heeled leather lace-ups with a contrasting band, or saddle, across the instep. The classic version is white with a black or dark saddle. They are worn to give an outfit a retro, preppy or 1950s-inspired look.

Because the contrast color draws the eye to the foot, they work as a statement piece in a styled outfit. They are associated with 1940s and 1950s school fashion and later appeared in pop culture, where they have also signaled a quirky or nerdy style.

paras: They are worn like any casual oxford with trousers, rolled jeans, skirts or vintage-style outfits. Choosing a color pairing (black on white is the standard, with brown or navy saddles also common) sets how bold the look is.
No health risks are specific to the style. Like other flat, low-heeled leather shoes they offer little arch or cushioning unless fitted with insoles, and the white leather shows scuffs.

angle.text: Saddle shoes are worn to add a vintage, collegiate or retro accent to an outfit. The contrast panel makes the shoe a focal point of the look.

lead: Saddle shoes, also called saddle oxfords, are casual low-heeled leather shoes with a plain toe and a saddle-shaped panel across the middle of the foot. The standard color scheme is white with a black, dark brown or dark blue saddle, though other pairings exist [1].

For someone styling their appearance, the two-tone contrast is the point: it adds a retro or collegiate accent to an outfit and visually frames the foot. They are most associated with the 1940s and 1950s, when they were typical school footwear for girls, and were worn by men and women in versions from golf shoes to uniform shoes [1].
In pop culture they have appeared as part of Steve Urkel's nerdy look in Family Matters and in the 2013 film Stoker [1].
infobox: White with black, brown or navy saddle

paras: The shoe is a plain-toe oxford with a leather saddle, a band across the middle of the foot, in a contrasting color to the body [1].
Saddle shoes were especially linked to the 1940s and 1950s as schoolgirl footwear and are filed under 1950s fashion. Variants have been made for men and women and in sporting styles such as golf [1].

timeline.event: Peak association with school and youth fashion [1].
